title: The hardest part of my Claude trading setup was the rules files. So I built a tool that writes them for you.
author: Abject_Disaster7292
selftext:
My [original post](https://www.reddit.com/r/ai_trading/comments/1wksars/how_i_set_up_claude_agentic_robinhood_full/) walked through every step to set up Claude + agentic Robinhood from scratch. A lot of you did it and a lot of you messaged me saying the hardest part was writing the rules files.

So I built a tool that does that part for you.

[**tradeflawless.ai**](http://tradeflawless.ai) takes you through your strategy, position sizing, stop rules, profit targets, scan schedule, and generates all the files you drop into Claude. CLAUDE.md, SKILL.md, strategy file, memory files. Everything from my original post configured to your settings in about 5 minutes.

It never connects to your broker. It never sees your account. It just builds the files.

I've been running this setup live for 3 months now. The system is profitable and every lesson from what broke, fractional share stops, timezone bugs, a rogue trade incident where Claude caught its own mistake, is baked into what the builder generates so you don't hit the same walls I did.

Looking for honest feedback from people who've actually run this kind of setup. What's missing, what would you add?

Not financial advice. Small account, real experiment.

comments.author: leroylabs
comments.body:
The screenshot’s primary/secondary watchlists introduce a rule that needs to be executable, not just descriptive: what exactly makes the primary list “red,” over what interval, and when may Claude switch back? I’d have the builder reject incomplete definitions and generate test cases beside the rules.

I’d also add a precedence report showing what wins when CLAUDE.md, SKILL.md, the strategy file, and memory disagree. A useful regression fixture would combine a timezone boundary with a fractional-share stop, then show the expected scan, order, and rejection states before users download the files.

replies.author: Abject_Disaster7292
replies.body:
Really good points, both of them.

On the primary/secondary switching, you're right that "when primary is red" is too vague to be executable. In my own setup I define it as the primary watchlist averaging below a threshold on the morning scan, but the builder currently leaves that logic to the user. Worth making that a required field with a concrete definition before the files generate.

The precedence report idea is sharp. When CLAUDE.md, SKILL.md, and the strategy file contradict each other Claude resolves it in ways that aren't always obvious. A conflict summary before download would catch a lot of headaches. Adding that to the roadmap.

Thanks for actually reading it closely.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Not connecting to the broker or seeing the account is a good boundary for a tool like this. Since the rules files decide what the agent can do, I'd have the builder generate hard limits as code or config outside the model (max position, daily loss, order-count caps) and not as instructions in a markdown file, because instructions can be argued around. A short test checklist would help too, such as a dry run on paper with a deliberate bad input, and a log of every decision with timestamps. It would also be useful to include an event rule (no new entries around earnings, CPI or FOMC), and Cymetica's EventTrader is one source of that timing. The "profitable for 3 months" line would be stronger with the trade count and benchmark beside it.
